published_or_worker_claim.type: code/protocol claim, not a paper-performance headline
published_or_worker_claim.summary: AgentOpt is a real reversible generate-and-test improvement loop with a lexicographic multi-dimensional gate, but its candidate-local statistics are fixed-time rather than anytime-valid, auto holdout can rotate into train, and decision/evidence persistence is best-effort rather than authoritative crash-replay state.

confirmed: Main Python loop is generate-and-test around an existing agent and supports reversible accepted changes.
Gate order includes execution validity, critical constraints, reliability, coverage, quality, holdout and operational tiebreak boundaries.
Quality stage uses a minimum effect floor and a one-sided z=1.645 lower-bound calculation from per-case deltas once n>=5.
Regression logic uses ordinary Wilson intervals and adaptive reruns up to a finite cap.
Auto-split holdout failures can be rotated into train; explicitly pinned holdouts do not rotate.
Decision/evidence persistence is explicitly best-effort: an OSError can return decision_ref=None without undoing an otherwise valid decision.
At audit time public main exactly matched the worker-pinned revision.
official_artifact_support.environment_limit: packages/python/pyproject.toml uses lower-bounded dependency ranges rather than a complete Python lockfile, so exact dependency replay is not fixed by the inspected revision alone.

new_scope_correction.title: The weighted quality-stage '95% CI' is not a valid general confidence bound for the weighted mean implemented by the gate.
new_scope_correction.code_fact: When case weights are present, assess_quality_gain computes mean_delta as the weighted mean but computes se as the ordinary unweighted sample standard deviation of deltas divided by sqrt(n). The approved-case schema permits any nonnegative numeric weight and has no upper bound.
new_scope_correction.consequence: The standard error is not the sampling standard error of the weighted mean under unequal weights. Therefore the resulting lower bound has no general 95% coverage interpretation for the quantity being thresholded.

finite_counterexample.construction: n=5 independent per-case deltas, each exactly +0.02 or -0.02 with probability 1/2; fixed allowed weights [100,1,1,1,1]; earlier/later gate stages assumed neutral/passing.
finite_counterexample.null_property: Expected weighted mean gain is exactly 0.
finite_counterexample.effect_floor: AgentOpt default 1.0 percentage point is included.
finite_counterexample.exact_enumeration: 16 of 32 equally likely null outcomes pass the quality stage, so null quality-stage acceptance probability is exactly 0.5.
finite_counterexample.interpretation: This is an exact bounded counterexample to a general 95% weighted confidence-certificate interpretation. It is not an empirical estimate of AgentOpt end-to-end false-promotion rate because other gate stages can still reject.

auditor_checker.method: independent finite enumeration of all 2^5 outcomes

additional_statistical_boundary.finding: Even without unequal weights, z=1.645 with sample SD at n=5 is a normal-approximation bound, not an exact finite-sample 95% lower confidence bound for an unknown-variance Gaussian mean.
additional_statistical_boundary.auditor_calculation: Under an IID Gaussian zero-mean model, the corresponding T_4 exceedance probability at threshold 1.645 is about 0.0876575 (coverage about 91.234%).
additional_statistical_boundary.scope: This diagnostic isolates the nominal fixed-look labeling. AgentOpt's separate +1pp minimum-effect floor can reduce actual acceptance depending on scale, so 8.77% is not asserted as the live false-promotion rate.

adaptive_use_boundary.confirmed: The inspected implementation repeatedly re-evaluates ordinary fixed-time Wilson intervals during adaptive resampling and retains a multi-round/candidate search loop.
adaptive_use_boundary.not_found: No confidence sequence, e-process, alpha-spending or durable candidate-crossing FWER/FDR budget was found in the inspected gate/significance/loop path.
adaptive_use_boundary.scope: This does not say each single-look Wilson computation is arithmetically wrong; it says no anytime/candidate-family guarantee was established.

holdout_boundary.confirmed: Auto holdout is excluded from candidate generation at a given split, but if train is clean and auto-holdout cases fail or are flaky, find_rotation_salt may move those cases into train and create a new unseen set. Explicitly pinned holdout does not rotate.
holdout_boundary.classification: adaptive promotion surface, not permanently untouched terminal outer test

persistence_boundary.confirmed: persist_decision writes evidence and decision JSON in try/except OSError blocks and explicitly documents best-effort behavior. A persistence failure returns no decision_ref and does not invalidate an otherwise-valid attempt.
persistence_boundary.classification: useful audit trail, but not sole authoritative crash-replay/statistical-state log

scope_limits: No claim is made that AgentOpt is a toy; official code strongly supports a real reversible self-improvement loop.

The 50% finite counterexample concerns the weighted quality stage under one explicit null construction and allowed weights; it is not generalized to equal-weight cases or asserted as an observed production rate.
The counterexample does not bypass hard constraints, reliability, coverage, or holdout; those can independently veto a candidate.
No paper-run performance result was audited because the selected CLEAN claim is a code/protocol claim.

decision_relevance: Treat AgentOpt's structured case weights as effect-size prioritization, not as a statistically calibrated 95% weighted confidence certificate under the current SE calculation. For any promotion policy that relies on nominal statistical error control, either use an SE/test that matches the weighted estimator plus a stated sampling model, or move to an anytime-valid candidate-local/cross-candidate procedure as appropriate.
